chunks.text: # About CSUB Official sources: - https://www.csub.edu/about/ - https://www.csub.edu/about/facts.shtml - https://www.csub.edu/50/50-fun-facts-about-csub.shtml - https://www.csub.edu/av/ ## What is CSUB? CSUB stands for California State University, Bakersfield. It is a public university in the California State University (CSU) system in the southern San Joaquin Valley. It is not an abbreviation for a technical term such as "computer subsystem." CSUB is the only public university within nearly 100 miles. It is fully accredited by the Western Association of Schools and Colleges, Senior College and University Commission (WSCUC) and is a designated Hispanic-Serving Institution (HSI). Many students are the first in their families to attend college. - Main campus: 9001 Stockdale Highway, Bakersfield, CA 93311-1022 - Phone: (661) 654-CSUB (661-654-2782) - Website: https://www.csub.edu - Campus size: about 375 acres (formerly agricultural land) - Motto: `Runners on the rise! - Mascot: the Roadrunner (Rowdy) - School colors: blue and gold - Community nicknames: Roadrunners or `Runners There is also a satellite campus, CSUB Antelope Valley, in Lancaster. ## History The CSU system authorized CSUB in 1965 (the year on the university seal). The original name was California State College, Bakersfield. First classes were held on October 1, 1970. The campus earned university status in 1987. The CSU system itself was established through the Donahoe Higher Education Act of 1960. Dorothy Donahoe Hall on campus is named after Assemblywoman Dorothy Donahoe of Bakersfield. The main library is the Walter W. Stiern Library, named for State Senator Walter W. Stiern, who helped establish the campus. ## Academics Students can major in undergraduate and graduate degree programs across four academic colleges: - Arts and Humanities - Business and Public Administration - Natural Sciences, Mathematics and Engineering - Social Sciences and Education The university offers dozens of undergraduate and graduate programs, plus education credential programs and doctoral programs in educational leadership and nursing practice. Men: Baseball, Basketball, Soccer, Swimming and Diving, Track and Field, Wrestling Women: Basketball, Beach Volleyball, Cross Country, Golf, Soccer, Softball, Swimming and Diving, Track and Field, Volleyball Campus life includes a Student Recreation Center, many student clubs and organizations, NCAA games, and on-campus events. The student newspaper is The Runner. San Joaquin kit foxes live on the Bakersfield campus. Dens can be in open areas; collared foxes are part of population monitoring. ## Antelope Valley campus CSUB Antelope Valley is in Lancaster, on the northeast corner of Antelope Valley College (J-8 and 30th Street West). - Address: 43909 30th Street West, Lancaster, CA 93536 - Phone: (661) 952-5000 - Email: csubav@csub.edu - Website: https://www.csub.edu/av/ It is a branch campus offering bachelor's, master's, and teacher credential programs so students can stay in the Antelope Valley. Office hours change; check the AV website. ## Contacts - Main campus phone: (661) 654-2782 - Website: https://www.csub.edu

# Grades and graduation Official sources: - https://catalog.csub.edu/policies-procedures/academic-policies/undergraduate/academic-affairs-academic-programs/ - https://www.csub.edu/registrar/_files/Graduation-Checklist-for-UGRD-LH.pdf - https://www.csub.edu/registrar/grades.shtml - Registrar: https://www.csub.edu/registrar/ and (661) 654-3036 ## Can I graduate with a D? Yes — possibly, but it depends on which GPA and requirement the D affects. Graduation requires a minimum overall GPA of 2.00 (C) and a minimum of 2.00 in the major, the minor (if applicable), and CSUB coursework. Only letter-graded courses (A, B, C, D, F, with plus/minus) are used in GPA computation. A D is a passing grade (1.0 points); it does not automatically block graduation. Students cannot graduate with grades of I (Incomplete), RP (Report in Progress), or RD (Report Delayed) on their record. Those pending grades must be changed before the degree can be awarded. Some specific requirements must be met with specified grades. GWAR by course requires a C- or better (or GWAR by exam with a score of 8 or higher). A D would not satisfy GWAR by course, or any other requirement that explicitly needs a C- or better. Therefore: - If the D keeps your overall GPA and required GPAs (major, minor, CSUB) at or above 2.00, you may still meet the GPA requirement for graduation. - If the D causes any required GPA to fall below 2.00, you would need to raise that GPA (for example by repeating the course if allowed, or earning higher grades in other courses) to reach the 2.00 minimum. - If the course with a D is being used to satisfy a requirement that explicitly requires a C- or better (for example, GWAR by course), a D would not satisfy that requirement. - You cannot graduate with pending I, RP, or RD grades on your record. If you want specific guidance for your record, consult your academic advisor or the Registrar to see how that D affects your major, minor, overall, and CSUB GPA and whether repeating the course or other actions are needed. ## GPA requirements Graduation requires a minimum overall

Only letter-graded courses (A, B, C, D, F, with plus/minus) count in GPA. D is passing (1.0 points). ## Incomplete and pending grades Students cannot graduate with I (Incomplete), RP (Report in Progress), or RD (Report Delayed) on their record. Pending grades must be resolved before the degree is awarded. ## GWAR The Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement (GWAR) by course requires a grade of C- or better. A D does not satisfy GWAR by course. GWAR may also be met by exam with a score of 8 or higher.

# Walter W. Stiern Library Official hours: https://csub.libguides.com/library/hours and https://csub.libcal.com/hours/ Library home: https://www.csub.edu/library/ Hours change for holidays, finals, and summer. Always verify on the official hours page. ## Library hours (Fall 2026 regular schedule) Typical hours during Fall 2026 (after summer session ended): - Sunday: 12:00 PM – 8:00 PM - Monday–Thursday: 8:00 AM – 10:00 PM - Friday: 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM - Saturday: 11:00 AM – 5:00 PM Labor Day (Monday, September 7, 2026): library closed. Veterans Day (Wednesday, November 11, 2026): library closed. Thanksgiving: closed Thursday–Friday, November 26–27, 2026. On Wednesday, November 25 the library is listed as closed (closes at 5:00 PM on the hours calendar). Extended hours near finals (late November into mid-December 2026): some weeknights extend to midnight (8:00 AM – 12:00 AM). Check LibCal for the exact finals-week dates. Summer session hours (when in effect) have been Monday–Thursday 8:00 AM – 6:00 PM, closed Friday–Sunday. Fall 2026 is not on summer hours. ## 24-hour study room The 24-hour study room and lockers are on the lower level of the Walter W. Stiern Library, near the lower entrance. A valid Runner ID is required for after-hours access. This room is typically open 24 hours even when the main library is closed, except on some holidays (for example Labor Day and Thanksgiving). Group study rooms: https://csub.libcal.com/reserve ## Research help - 24/7 research chat is available through the library website - In-person research help during Fall 2026: Monday–Thursday 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM, Friday 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM; weekends use 24/7 chat - Check-out desk: (661) 654-3172 - Library administration: (661) 654-3042 - Email: csub@calstate.libanswers.com ## Antelope Valley Campus Library - Monday–Thursday: 9:00 AM – 8:00 PM - Friday: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM - Saturday–Sunday: closed - Closed on Labor Day and Veterans Day
